Quick note: the table you provided contains 23 models but I count 11 failing models (not 14). I proceeded using the actual results in the table and grouped those 11 failures below.

1) Categorize failures
- Category: Provider-deprecated (404 Not Found)
  - Models: gemini-1.5-pro, gemini-1.5-flash, gpt-3.5-turbo, claude-2.1
  - What the error means / likely cause: The provider is returning 404 for the model id — the model identifier is no longer available (provider-deprecation, rename, or removed API surface). Likely caused by provider-side deprecation/retirement or our config using old model IDs.

- Category: Authentication / Authorization (401 Unauthorized)
  - Models: mistral-medium, codestral
  - What the error means / likely cause: The provider rejected the API key/token. Likely causes: expired/rotated API key, wrong credentials loaded in secrets store, missing header/scopes, or provider-side account problem.

- Category: Provider upstream down (503 Service Unavailable)
  - Models: deepseek-chat, deepseek-reasoner
  - What the error means / likely cause: Provider or their upstream services are temporarily unavailable. Likely cause: vendor outage, deployment/service crash, or rate-limiting/back-end failure.

- Category: Connection timeout
  - Models: qwen-turbo, qwen-plus
  - What the error means / likely cause: The test client could not complete a TCP/HTTP request in 30s. Likely causes: network/firewall/DNS issues between runner and provider, provider slow/unresponsive, or incorrect endpoint causing routing problems.

- Category: Bad request — invalid model name (400 Bad Request)
  - Models: phi-3-mini (Azure)
  - What the error means / likely cause: The request was syntactically valid but the endpoint does not accept that model name — likely mis-specified Azure deployment name, wrong region/endpoint, or incorrect model identifier for the Azure endpoint.

2) Prioritized fix plan (per category)
- Provider-deprecated (404)
  - Immediate action: Disable these model IDs from the smoke-test config (stop sending traffic), confirm deprecation notices in provider docs, identify supported replacement model(s), and open a ticket/PR to remove or replace the models in config. Notify product owners/consumers that referenced models are EoL.
  - Time estimate: 1–4 hours to disable and push config + smoke test; 0.5–2 days to validate and roll in replacements across consumers.
  - Owner: Platform/API integration team (with product-owner input and vendor liaison).
  - Priority: High — remove from tests immediately to stop repetitive 404 alerts.

- Authentication (401)
  - Immediate action: Validate which credential is used (secret manager), run quick curl/test with current key to confirm, check provider console for key status, rotate/regenerate key if expired, update secret store, then rerun smoke-test.
  - Time estimate: 15–120 minutes if keys are simply expired; up to a day if account re-provisioning or vendor support is required.
  - Owner: Infra/Secrets team (with Platform/API team contact).
  - Priority: High — typically quick to fix but blocks those models until resolved.

- Provider upstream down (503)
  - Immediate action: Check provider status page & logs, open vendor support ticket, add retries/backoff and a circuit-breaker in production routing to avoid repeated 503 cascades, and temporarily remove the models from production routing if critical.
  - Time estimate: 1–4 hours to implement mitigations and open support/monitor; vendor fix time is variable (hours–days).
  - Owner: Platform/Integration + Vendor liaison.
  - Priority: Medium-High — service-impacting but may be transient.

- Connection timeout (30s)
  - Immediate action: From the smoke-test host run curl/traceroute/DNS lookups against the provider endpoint, check firewall rules, try extending timeout to 60s for diagnostics, and open a ticket with provider if endpoint is reachable but slow. Validate endpoint URL / port correctness.
  - Time estimate: 1–4 hours to triage root cause; longer if network team or provider must intervene.
  - Owner: Infra/Network + Platform team.
  - Priority: Medium — could be network misconfiguration or provider slowness.

- Bad Request — invalid model name (400)
  - Immediate action: Verify the Azure endpoint and the exact deployment/model name mapping (Azure uses deployment names rather than generic model ids), update configuration to the correct deployment name/region and re-run tests. If model not deployed, deploy or request the deployment.
  - Time estimate: 30–120 minutes.
  - Owner: Cloud (Azure) team / Platform integration.
  - Priority: High — usually a quick config fix.

Cross-cutting immediate steps (apply now)
- Disable failing models in the nightly smoke-test to stop alert noise until they are fixed (2–10 minutes).
- Re-run smoke-tests for verification immediately after any fix.
- Create tickets (or update existing) per model with the above recommended owner and link provider logs/status pages.

3) Removal recommendations
| Model | Action | Reason |
|-------|--------|--------|
| gpt-4o | Keep | Passing and reasonable latency (412ms) — keep as a flagship OpenAI model. |
| gpt-4o-mini | Keep | Passing and fast (287ms) — useful low-latency variant. |
| gpt-4-turbo | Keep | Passing and widely used; keep. |
| o1 | Keep (review) | Passing but very slow (8341ms) — investigate routing/latency; keep after review. |
| o3-mini | Keep | Passing (1203ms); acceptable but higher latency than mini variants. |
| claude-opus-4 | Keep | Passing; keep. |
| claude-sonnet-4 | Keep | Passing; keep. |
| claude-haiku-3-5 | Keep | Passing and fast — keep. |
| gemini-2.0-flash | Keep | Passing; keep. |
| gemini-1.5-pro | Remove | 404 Not Found — provider-deprecated model id; remove from config. |
| gemini-1.5-flash | Remove | 404 Not Found — provider-deprecated; remove. |
| gpt-3.5-turbo | Remove | 404 Not Found — deprecated or wrong id for this integration; remove from config and replace with supported model if needed. |
| claude-2.1 | Remove | 404 Not Found — deprecated; remove from config. |
| mistral-large | Keep | Passing; keep. |
| mistral-medium | Keep (fix) | 401 Unauthorized — likely expired/invalid API key; restore credentials. |
| codestral | Keep (fix) | 401 Unauthorized — same auth problem; fix credentials. |
| llama-3.3-70b | Keep | Passing and fast; keep. |
| llama-3.1-8b | Keep | Passing and fast; keep. |
| deepseek-chat | Keep (fix) | 503 Service Unavailable — vendor upstream outage; keep but monitor and escalate to vendor. |
| deepseek-reasoner | Keep (fix) | 503 Service Unavailable — vendor outage; keep but fix. |
| qwen-turbo | Keep (fix) | Connection timeout — network/endpoint problem; triage network and provider. |
| qwen-plus | Keep (fix) | Connection timeout — triage network or provider. |
| phi-3-mini | Keep (fix) | 400 Bad Request — invalid model name for endpoint (Azure deployment/name mismatch); correct config or deployment. |

Notes on removals: I recommend permanently removing the four 404-deprecated models (gemini-1.5-pro, gemini-1.5-flash, gpt-3.5-turbo, claude-2.1) from the active config and replacing them with supported alternatives if needed. For everything else, prefer fixing credentials/configuration or triaging vendor/network issues before considering removal.

4) Passing model notes / concerns
- Count: 12 models in the table show PASS (not 9). If you intended a different count, please confirm.
- Unusually slow: o1 is an outlier at ~8.3s (8341ms) — investigate routing, region, or model load; o3-mini at ~1.2s is borderline compared to other mini variants. If these slownesses affect user flows, consider switching traffic or investigating provider-side throttling.
- Redundancy: We have many models from the same providers:
  - OpenAI: gpt-4o, gpt-4o-mini, gpt-4-turbo, o1, o3-mini — consider reducing to 2 representative OpenAI models for routine smoke tests (one high-capacity and one low-latency/cost option).
  - Anthropic: three variants (opus, sonnet, haiku) — acceptable for coverage but consolidate if test run duration/cost is a concern.
  - Groq Llama models are fast and useful as low-latency alternatives.
- Recommendation: For nightly smoke tests keep one small & one flagship model per provider as representatives; run a weekly or scheduled full sweep across all configured models to catch provider-specific regressions. Also add a latency threshold check (e.g., warn if >2s median or >5s p95) so slow models (like o1) are flagged automatically.

5) 3-sentence executive summary
The nightly smoke run shows 11 failing models grouped into five root causes: four provider-deprecated (404), two auth failures (401), two vendor outages (503), two network timeouts, and one Azure misconfigured model (400). Immediate priorities: remove the four deprecated models from config, restore/rotate credentials for Mistral entries, open vendor tickets for Deepseek and Alibaba timeouts, and correct the Azure model name; fixes range from minutes (credential/config) to vendor-dependent timelines (hours–days). I recommend permanently removing the deprecated models and keeping the rest while treating auth/timeouts/upstream issues as high priority to fix.

If you want, I can:
- open the tickets/PRs for disabling/removing the deprecated IDs,
- prepare the exact commands and curl checks for the 401/timeout/400 triage steps,
- or propose a reduced representative model list for the smoke-test to reduce flakiness and cost. Which would you like me to do next?
